I was in Burger King this week and was pleased to see that their drink dispenser machine was running KDE... I wonder if they'll switch to using Silverblue now and get a more reliable setup.

Almost anything you want to do in Gnome touches a spec or design that someone made there and has some obscure thing that kills it entirely... contrast this with my time as a KDE developer... it's night and day.

Interestingly, I've tried KDE multiple times on different devices & each time there's a Wifi issue that's not present in any other linux desktop. Even the steam deck's default steamos has this issue in desktop mode.
Libadwaita is a horrible design language. It wastes so much space, the disparity between gtk3/4 hurts the eyes and you pretty much depend on extensions for the most basic of things.
Fedora 39 KDE Spin has been flawless so far, and I love the window tiling native support. Also, suspend on Nvidia works again for me.
I've tried a variety of linucies, but I keep coming back to Fedora. It frequently works the best 'out of the box'... My biggest complaint is nvidia's drivers, but that's not unique to Fedora.
In my case, Fedora became collateral damage after the CentOS/RHEL drama. I've switched all my personal systems to Debian.
only Arch seems to be the smoothest. I'm running EndeavourOS... Fedora always freezes for minutes when the RAM is full. I'm thinking maybe it's ZRAM fault here?
Unfortunately I cannot switch to Fedora on my desktop, mainly because of lack of support of Adobe, missing 10bit support and CUDA. Linux is not mature for professional work in audiovisual production.

My experience with Fedora ended quickly, after installing it in the VBox... Every second letter of any text had been invisible and the whole DE was blinking at a rate of the mouse move speed... Went back to Ubuntu and Xubuntu.
I've been using Chrome directly under Wayland... and the rate of bugs is definitely higher than the Chrome team would tolerate on Windows or Mac.

Cool roadmap, but a focus on Flatpak basically turns me away from ever having a use for the distro now... It's death by a thousand papercuts with Flatpak, all in exchange for a modicum of developer convenience.
Over flatpaks and snaps, I choose Nix... Actually, every single bullet point they mentioned is solved in NixOS.

And there are many small innovations ticking into Fedora, activated by default: zram, fstrim, earlyoom/systemd-oomd, systemd-resolved, btrfs+compression... In comparison, Debian in the standard installation feels lacking behind.

I chose popos, because the second I wanted discord or Spotify on fedora I had to go through a whole page of commands to do it, and it didn't quite run correctly. When I installed some GUI apps on fedora, they wouldn't show up on the start menu.
Having used both on a regular basis, I hope they stick with GNOME. KDE is highly-configurable, which brings about a level of fun, but otherwise somewhat unpolished and at least a bit more buggy.

The fact that you need extensions for something as simple as dock functionality is insane... The fact that all my extensions get broken for a month after every single release is downright infuriating.
People may not like it, it may not be space efficient as some GNOME themes or macOS, but that thing works, doesn't crash, and improves productivity.
Although Wayland is more modern, it's been nothing but trouble for me on older hardware. I'd prefer non-smooth scrolling any day over a computer screen that doesn't come back after sleep.

The last time I tried Wayland, I noticed that picture-in-picture in Firefox didn't work correctly because Wayland doesn't allow applications to say 'this window should show up on top of all other windows.'
